rules.statement: Where a will and a codicil are both missing but only one is found, it may be inferred that the testator revoked the will by mistake or ignorance, leaving the codicil valid.
rules.supporting_quote: I find on the evidence that the will was in the possession of the testator, and that it was not forthcoming at his death. The presumption is that he destroyed it. I think it is very probable that the deceased did wish to revoke both the will and the codicil, but by mistake or ignorance only destroyed one of these documents. If the will had been in existence, it seems to me very probable that it would have been found as the codicil was found. I find them on the issue that the last will was revoked, but the codicil was not revoked. I see no reason why the codicil should not be admitted to probate. It is an independent document, and its provisions can be carried out apart from those of the will. I make order accordingly, and order letters of administration with the codicil annexed to issue to the. applicant, the eldest son of the deceased. The second respondent
